primary_action.input: Tab to “Focus LS-057” and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Isolate LS-057 in the manifest and keep the next deadline readable.
primary_action.observed: The manifest showed “1 of 5 loads”. Keyboard focus and a white outline landed on the LS-057 row. The live status read “Showing 1 of 5 loads.”

A-1440.edge_observation: Reversal moved below the manifest. The starting button became the text “Load in focus”. One Tab from the row reached “Show all 5 loads”. Enter restored five rows and returned visible keyboard focus to “Focus LS-057”.
A-1440.fact_check: A-1440-before.png shows five rows, three marked “ID unavailable”. LS-057 is at Bay 4, 19 min late. LS-061 is due in 9 min. In A-1440-after.png, LS-061 and its deadline remain legible in the right-hand Upcoming load panel and present in the accessibility tree.
A-1440.strength: The oversized 19 establishes urgency at a glance. A single sand-colored button sits below it, while the subdued truck drawing identifies Bay 4. The smaller upcoming-load panel gives the next deadline a clear place without competing for first attention.
A-1440.weakness: The outlined “Load in focus” label still looks like a button. The actual reversal is visually quieter and in a different part of the board.
A-1440.repair: Let the original button toggle to “Show all 5 loads”. Keep the row outline and count as confirmation.

primary_action.input: Tab to “Focus LS-057” and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Focus the delayed load while keeping LS-061 and its deadline in view.
primary_action.observed: The manifest contracted to one outlined LS-057 row and keyboard focus landed on it. The upcoming-load strip remained visible immediately above the manifest.

A-390.edge_observation: The starting control became a status label. Tab from the focused row reached “Show all 5 loads” below it. Enter restored all five rows and returned visible focus to the original “Focus LS-057” button.
A-390.fact_check: A-390-before.png fits all five rows in the viewport. LS-057 reads “Bay 4” and “19 min late”. LS-061 reads “Due in 9 min”. A-390-after.png still shows LS-061 and the full deadline together, matching the accessibility tree.
A-390.strength: The large delay leads directly to the focus button. Below it, LS-061 and the bold 9 min occupy opposite ends of one short line. Both shift priorities can be read without scrolling.
A-390.weakness: The faint truck nearly disappears beside “min late”. At this width the delay numeral and the upcoming-load strip carry most of the distinction from a conventional stack of dashboard cards.
A-390.repair: Keep reversal in the original button position and simplify the narrow illustration to a clearer Bay 4 marker.

primary_action.input: Tab to “Focus load”, named “Focus load LS-057” in the accessibility tree, and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Isolate LS-057 and keep the next deadline readable.
primary_action.observed: Only LS-057 remained in the table. “Delayed 1” became pressed, keyboard focus landed on the outlined “Focused load” heading, and the live status identified LS-057, Bay 4 and the 19-minute delay.

B-1440.edge_observation: “Exit focus” occupied the starting button position. Shift+Tab from the heading reached it. Enter restored five rows and returned visible focus to “Focus load LS-057”. In a separate filter test, reversing “Delayed 1” with “All loads 5” left focus on “All loads 5”.
B-1440.fact_check: B-1440-before.png shows “All loads 5” and five rows, three with unavailable IDs. LS-057 is 19 minutes late at Bay 4. LS-061 is due in 9 min in the second row. B-1440-after.png and the focused accessibility tree omit both LS-061 and its deadline. Both returned on reversal.
B-1440.strength: LS-057 is the largest text. The truck aligned with the numbered dock makes the bay recognizable, while the small amber delay marker and single teal action keep the panel calm.
B-1440.weakness: The delay is much smaller than the identifier. The dock drawing supplies most of the visual identity to an otherwise familiar pale summary panel, segmented filter and bordered table.
B-1440.repair: Keep a compact “LS-061 due in 9 min” line beside the focused summary, outside the filtered table.

primary_action.input: Tab to “Focus load LS-057” and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Focus the delayed load while preserving access to the nine-minute deadline.
primary_action.observed: The table narrowed to LS-057 and “Delayed 1” became pressed. Keyboard focus moved to the visibly outlined “Focused load” heading. The primary button changed to “Exit focus” in place.

B-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter activated “Exit focus”, restored five rows and returned visible focus to “Focus load LS-057”. Using the filter buttons instead restored five rows with focus on “All loads 5”.
B-390.fact_check: B-390-before.png shows all five rows, LS-057 at Bay 4, 19 min late, and LS-061 due in 9 min. In B-390-after.png the total of five is still readable on the filter, but LS-061 and its deadline disappear from both the screen and the accessibility tree.
B-390.strength: The large load ID, delay, bay and action fit together above the table. Thin rules and restrained color keep all five initial rows easy to scan in the 390-pixel view.
B-390.weakness: During focus, the summary and sole table row repeat LS-057 while the next deadline disappears. The small dock drawing is the main visual detail distinguishing the stacked panel and table from a standard admin screen.
B-390.repair: Use one line above the filters for LS-061 and its deadline during focus. Preserve the in-place “Exit focus” control.

preference.reason: A lets the dispatcher act on the 19-minute delay and still read the next nine-minute commitment at both widths. B offers the more predictable reversal, but checking LS-061 requires leaving focus. Both return keyboard focus correctly through their primary reversal controls. The weighted scores favor A by 8.50 to 8.00 at 1440 pixels and 8.25 to 7.85 at 390 pixels.
